items.s: Imagine a city that ____ 170 kilometres long.
The Line ____ as part of NEOM.
Designers ____ a completely new way of life.
Nobody ____ a city of this size in a straight line before.
In May 2026, a report ____ that major work had been put off.

tfn.s: Construction workers have been sent home.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say what happened to the builders or workers.

tfn.s: The Line forms part of a larger plan called NEOM.
tfn.why: The text says: "The Line was introduced as part of NEOM, a large plan to develop an area in the north-west of the country."

tfn.s: The Line was planned to be 170 kilometres long.
tfn.why: The text says: "Imagine a city that is 170 kilometres long but only a short distance across."

tfn.s: The project was officially cancelled in May 2026.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "That did not mean the entire project had officially been cancelled."

tfn.s: Fast transport would take residents from one part of the city to another in about an hour.
tfn.why: The text says transport would carry residents across the city "in minutes".

normal, not special

focus.note: A linking word joins two ideas. Use but for a difference, so for a result, and because for a reason.

items.s: The pictures looked wonderful, ____ building the real city is very hard.

Work was put off ____ the cost was too high.

move an event to a later date

items.s: By the time the report was published, the early images ____ around the world.
Details of the new budget ____ yet.

When costs rose sharply, officials ____ to wait.

tfn.s: The Line's promoters expected most residents to depend on private cars.
tfn.why: The text says the plan offered "far less dependence on private cars".

tfn.s: The report established that the plan had been permanently abandoned.
tfn.why: The text says: "The report did not establish that every element of the plan had been permanently abandoned."

tfn.s: The delay was linked to a change in the Saudi authorities' spending priorities.
tfn.why: The text says further work was put back "as Saudi authorities reconsidered their spending priorities".

tfn.s: Investors have asked for their money back.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether investors have asked for their money back.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that a very long delay can weaken the idea behind a project.
tfn.why: The text says a project that slips by ten years "loses the technology and much of the enthusiasm it was designed around".

put one on top of another in a pile
made to advertise something
basic systems such as roads, power and water
money put into something to make a profit later
a new idea or way of doing something
in a way that is sensible about what can really happen

focus.note: Despite takes a noun phrase. Whereas introduces a contrast clause. Otherwise, therefore and unless each begin a new clause or sentence.

items.s: ____ the enormous costs, the government kept the project going for years.
Some people see the project as a bold risk, ____ others see it as a waste of money.

The two companies had become so ____ that nobody could say where one role ended and the other began.

Unwilling to follow ____ methods, the team built the bridge in an entirely new way.

match.d: stop work for now, to continue later

items.s: A growing sense of ____ surrounds the original timetable.

tfn.s: The writer treats the gap between announced ambitions and delivery as a problem found in other countries too.
tfn.why: The text calls it "a gap that is hardly unique to Saudi Arabia" and mentions megaprojects elsewhere.

tfn.s: The writer expects a project delayed by ten years to return to the same technologies and costs.
tfn.why: The text says such a scheme "re-emerges into a world whose technologies, costs and priorities have all moved on".

tfn.s: The cost of the project has risen by more than half since it was announced.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text gives no figures for the cost.

tfn.s: The text suggests that Semafor's report and an official cancellation amount to the same thing.
tfn.why: The text says the report "should not be confused with an official declaration" of cancellation.

tfn.s: The text treats the project's striking image as an achievement that did not settle whether it could be delivered.
tfn.why: It calls the image "a considerable achievement", but says the scale "complicated any credible assessment" of delivery.

focus.note: Notwithstanding and hence are followed by a noun phrase; albeit introduces a small concession. Nonetheless and whereas work across clauses or sentences.

items.s: The design was praised for its ambition, ____ with some reservations.

speak.title: Role-play: shrink the city or keep the dream
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You want to keep the full 170-kilometre plan. Explain why the idea is important. Answer your partner's worries and try to agree a plan.

b.text: You think the city is too costly. You want to make it smaller or wait until after 2030. Ask about the cost and offer a compromise.

phrases: We can't give up on this dream now.
What would that mean for the people who live there?
Could we start with a smaller version?
I'd rather wait than waste the money.
Let's agree on a plan we can both support.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you keep the big plan, shrink it or put it off, and why?
